title: AeroRec: an oracle-based diagnosis platform for bias propagation and debiasing boundaries in recommender systems
description:
AeroRec is a travel-recommendation platform built as a measurement instrument rather than a leaderboard entry. It runs a four-way recall → DeepFM ranking → five-step mixing pipeline with a graceful-degradation path, and wraps it in an oracle-based diagnostic harness in which the true CTR and the exposure propensity are known in closed form.

That construction makes two questions answerable that production logs cannot answer: (i) how exposure bias propagates through the recall / ranking / mixing stages, and (ii) under what conditions inverse-propensity-scoring (IPS/SNIPS) debiasing costs more variance than the bias it removes.

What this archive contains

  • the full source tree (pipeline, FastAPI service, Streamlit explainability panel, 133 automated tests);
  • seven bias-diagnosis experiment outputs under data/bias/ and four real-data validation outputs under data/real_validation/ (Criteo 1M, Criteo 200k with a 3-seed error bar, UCI Adult);
  • the preprint PDF and the six figures, each regenerable byte-for-byte from the committed JSONs by scripts/make_paper_figures.py;
  • a reproducibility CI workflow that re-runs the experiments and asserts the artifacts do not drift.

Headline findings

  • Bias primarily induces ranking reversal rather than a level shift: ranking-level Spearman falls from +0.87 to −0.51 as skew increases, while the naive level error stays flat.
  • Debiasing has an effective boundary in propensity space (ESS/N): above it, the gain is within the experiment's tolerance of zero; below it, the variance cost dominates. The threshold is reported as a conservative operating point derived from a coarse propensity grid, not as a precise crossing.
  • Replacing the closed-form propensity with a log-estimated one leaves SNIPS error essentially unchanged (|Δ| ≤ 0.0023), and the ESS/N warning remains fail-safe with respect to missed alarms.

Reproducing: see README.md and docs/paper/README.md. Every reported number is produced by a committed script from committed inputs.

Related work: this software accompanies the preprint Bias propagation and effective boundaries of debiasing in recommender systems: An oracle-based diagnosis study (Preprints 2026, 202610.2582), DOI 10.20944/preprints202610.2582.v1. The repository state that the preprint's numbers were produced from is tagged preprint-v1; this release adds archival metadata on top of that state and changes no code or result file.
notes: Provenance: code and result artifacts are identical to the git tag preprint-v1 (commit c41997b), which is the state the accompanying preprint was produced from. This release only adds CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json.
